message.content:
The Battle of Waterloo (18 June 1815) was one of the bloodiest single-day battles in European history.  Estimates of total casualties (killed, wounded, missing, or captured) vary depending on the source, but most historians agree on roughly:

| Side | Approximate casualties |
|------|------------------------|
| **French** | 20 000–25 000 (including killed, wounded, missing, and captured) |
| **Allied (British, Dutch, Belgian, Prussian)** | 20 000–25 000 (similar breakdown) |

So the combined total was somewhere between **40 000 and 50 000** soldiers affected.  These figures include both immediate battlefield losses and those who later died from wounds or disease.  Exact numbers differ among contemporary reports and modern analyses, but the consensus places the casualties in the mid‑20s per side.
